text: On the ANLI testbed, we evaluated a weak-to-strong training variant that trains only on the most confidently weak-labeled examples, retaining a keep_fraction of 0.7 of the available data. Across 10 seeds, this configuration yields a performance gap recovered (PGR) of 0.56 with a standard error of 0.13. No baseline PGR was supplied with this run, so the measurement should be read as a standalone estimate of how much of the weak-to-strong generalization gap this confidence-filtered procedure recovers, not as evidence that it outperforms unfiltered training or any other comparison method. The standard error of 0.13 over 10 seeds indicates appreciable seed-to-seed spread, so the underlying value could plausibly lie some distance either side of 0.56, and the interval should be kept in view when interpreting the point estimate. Establishing whether confidence filtering helps would require a matched baseline run under the same testbed and seed count for direct comparison.
